messages:
mira: incident-bot -> PagerDuty fired: PD alert P-1798 for runtime-router-prod high 95th latency (auto-escalation)
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert P-1798 triggered at 2026-03-14T12:05:21Z. Symptom: router latency spike > SLA threshold. Auto-resolve window 3m.
apparently: trying to include a small note here
sam (oncall): acked. looking at graphs — 95p jumped to ~720ms then dipped. any customer-facing errors? :thinking_face:
laura: checking SLO dashboards and logs, no increase in 5xxs in the last 10m. synthetic pings are fine.
dan: I see a short kube node throttle on routing pool A at 12:04:xx, CPU jumped from 30->95% for ~20s. could be noisy neighbor on that host.
mira: interesting — allocator autoscale also briefly rebalanced pods. might be transient cold-start KV-warmup activity after a deploy? did we deploy recently?
laura: no deploys in last hour. we did push a config change to the cache layer 30m ago but it was low-risk.
sam (oncall): running quick checks: `kubectl top pods -n runtime | grep router` and `/infra/ops/check-hosts --since 5m`
ops-bot: host-203 reaped high load, docker restart count 0, io wait spiked. Recommended: cordon host-203 until investigation.
dan: hmm, host-203 is in routing pool A. I'll move ephemeral traffic off it via weight=0 for pool A in routing config.
mira: nice. can you post the command you ran so I can add to the incident notes?
dan: ran: ```sh
redwoodctl routing adjust-weight --pool runtime-router-A --host host-203 --weight 0
``` done, routing rebalanced in ~7s.
sam (oncall): latency trending back down. PD auto-resolve window in 60s, but keep watching.
laura: confirmed 95p down to ~140ms, p50 steady. no 5xxs, no customer errors in logs.
mira: small customer-hit check: queried recent support tickets for runtime-related errors — none. CX flagged nothing.
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert P-1798 auto-resolved at 2026-03-14T12:07:43Z (no manual resolve).
sam (oncall): marking as brief noisy page. root cause likely host-level noisy CPU spike causing router tail latency. action: cordon host-203 and spin a replacement; infra to follow up and add host to maintenance.
laura: adding a short post-incident note in the oncall doc, tagging infra. no customer impact, no followup blameless post needed, but flagging for host stability triage.
mira: assigning follow-up to @dan and @infra-team. dan will file host-203 ticket with host metrics and suggested remediation.
dan: filing now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4621 — attaching cpu/io graphs. will propose kernel/firmware check + repro.
sam (oncall): thanks. I'll hand off to next oncall in 30m with notes. good quick clear.
laura: :thumbsup: closing thread unless anyone sees residuals.
mira: thanks all — good catch and smooth handoff. keeping this as a transient noisy alert (auto-resolved), will review suppression thresholds if these repeat.
